title: Terphenylthiolate-Ligated Lanthanide Terminal Methyl Complexes Form Crystallographically Characterizable Terminal Acyls and Trimethylcyclopropanetriolates from Carbon Monoxide

synthesis.procedure: Under argon (Schlenk or glovebox), La(SAr^iPr6)2I (0.25 g, 0.21 mmol) was dissolved in ca. 10 mL diethyl ether in a 20 mL vial, cooled to -78 °C, and methyllithium (0.16 mL of 1.6 M in diethyl ether, 0.25 mmol) was added over 1 min. The mixture was warmed to ambient temperature and stirred for 2 h. Solvent was removed under reduced pressure; the residue was extracted with ca. 10 mL hot hexane, centrifuged, and the supernatant filtered. Standing at -35 °C for 18 h gave X-ray-quality crystals. Crystalline yield 0.13 g (0.11 mmol, 53%).

synthesis.procedure: Prepared analogously to 1-La under argon. Nd(SAr^iPr6)2I (0.75 g, 0.58 mmol) in ca. 10 mL diethyl ether in a 20 mL vial was cooled to -78 °C and treated with methyllithium (0.38 mL of 1.6 M in diethyl ether, 0.61 mmol) over 1 min. After warming to ambient temperature and stirring for 2 h, the solvent was removed. The residue was extracted with ca. 10 mL hot hexane, centrifuged, filtered, and kept at -35 °C for 18 h to give crystals. Crystalline yield 0.50 g (0.42 mmol, 73%).

synthesis.procedure: Li-free 1-La (0.050 g, 0.040 mmol; checked by 7Li NMR) was dissolved in ca. 0.5 mL C6D6 in a J. Young NMR tube. The solution was frozen in liquid nitrogen, the headspace evacuated and replaced with carbon monoxide, then thawed, sealed, and shaken; this CO introduction was repeated twice more. After 2 h at ambient temperature, 1H NMR showed complete consumption of 1-La. Solvent was removed and the residue dissolved in about 0.5 mL hexane. Standing at ambient temperature for 3 h gave yellow crystals. Crystalline yield 0.036 g (0.030 mmol, 72%).

synthesis.procedure: Li-free 1-Nd (0.050 g, 0.040 mmol; checked by 7Li NMR) was dissolved in ca. 0.5 mL C6D6 in a J. Young NMR tube. The solution was frozen, the headspace replaced with carbon monoxide, thawed, sealed, and shaken; the CO introduction was repeated twice more. After 4 h at ambient temperature, 1H NMR showed complete consumption of 1-Nd. Solvent was removed and the residue dissolved in about 0.5 mL hexane. Standing at ambient temperature for 18 h gave green crystals. Crystalline yield 0.030 g (0.025 mmol, 62%).

synthesis.procedure: Crude 1-La containing residual LiI (“1-La·LiI”, 0.050 g) was dissolved in ca. 0.5 mL C6D6 in a J. Young NMR tube. The solution was frozen, the headspace replaced with CO, thawed, sealed, and shaken; this was repeated twice more. The solution turned bright yellow and then colorless after ca. 5 min. Solvent was removed and the residue recrystallized at ambient temperature from ca. 0.5 mL hexane, giving colorless crystals of 3-La together with (LiSAr^iPr6)2. An alternative route treated ca. 10 mg of 2-La in ca. 0.5 mL C6D6 with excess LiI (0.020 g, 0.15 mmol); the yellow solution faded over 30 min and 1H NMR indicated 3-La. Pure bulk samples were not isolated because of similar solubility of the lithium thiolate byproduct.

synthesis.procedure: In a manner similar to 3-La, crude 1-Nd containing residual LiI (“1-Nd·LiI”, 0.050 g) was dissolved in ca. 0.5 mL C6D6 in a J. Young NMR tube. The headspace was replaced with carbon monoxide by three freeze–evacuate–thaw cycles. The green solution darkened. Solvent was removed and the residue recrystallized at ambient temperature from ca. 0.5 mL hexane, giving blue crystals of 3-Nd together with (LiSAr^iPr6)2. Complete characterization was not possible because of the co-formed lithium thiolate.

synthesis.procedure: A sample of yellow 2-La was prepared in C6D6 in a J. Young NMR tube as described for 2-La and stored for 2 days at ambient temperature until the solution was colorless. Benzene was removed under reduced pressure and the residue extracted with ca. 0.5 mL hexane. After 18 h, a small amount of colorless crystals of the enolate complex 4-La had grown. No isolated mass yield is reported.
